The ''Outrider'' departed Lok for the next race on Rori without further trouble,<ref name="LS" /> but the Empire continued to monitor his activities and dispatched the [[Dark Jedi/Legends|Dark Jedi]] [[Namman Cha]] to Rori in the hopes of uncovering his contacts within the Alliance.<ref name="DS" />

[[File:Kor_Vella_Ambush.jpg|thumb|right|220px|Rendar is ambushed by Guri in Kor Vella.]]
The spacer hired by Rendar for security was oblivious about why the Empire was after the smuggler, but when the spacer tried to ask about the ''Outrider''{{'s}} cargo during the trip to Rori, Rendar politely reminded his companion that they were only employed to guard the ship, not to ask questions. Before the [[Narmle Memorial Rally]] got underway, Rendar met with two Rebel operatives at the starport, who took possession of the crate of body armor and gave him his next cargo, a shipment of [[Bacta/Legends|bacta]] kits, in return. After taking the bacta back to the ''Outrider'', Rendar left with Chyler's team and headed for the race.<ref name="LS" /> When the race began, Rendar quietly left the track and met with [[Coret Bhan]], a [[Major/Legends|major]] within the Rebel Alliance, behind one of the grandstands. As Rendar handed the [[Zabrak/Legends|Zabrak]] a small package, they were approached by the Imperial agent from Lok, who attempted to apprehend Bhan. When the Rebel resisted, the Imperial fled to report back to Cha.<ref name="DS" /> Later, while Rendar joined the racing team to celebrate Chyler's victory, Cha and a group of [[Sith Shadows]] approached the ''Outrider'' but were forced to retreat by Rendar's security. Rendar and Chyler returned moments later and the Corellian immediately saw signs of a fight near the ship and asked about what had happened. Despite his security once again saving his cargo, he still did not reveal that he was working for the Alliance.<ref name="LS" />

The racing season next took Rendar to [[Talus/Legends|Talus]] in the [[Corellian system/Legends|Corellian system]] for the [[Nashal River Race]], before the group moved on to [[Corellia/Legends|Corellia]] itself. While Chyler was busy preparing for the [[Agrilat Swamp Circuit]], Rendar and his security partner headed for the [[City/Legends|city]] of [[Kor Vella/Legends|Kor Vella]]. There, Rendar met with two [[Bothan Spynet/Legends|Bothan Spynet]] agents and talked to them about Imperial [[Datafile/Legends|datafiles]] and some battle plans they were after. The [[Bothan/Legends|Bothans]] warned Rendar that they were being tailed, but before they could make it back to the ''Outrider'', he and the spacer were confronted by a group of Black Sun thugs led by Xizor's lieutenant, Guri, whose employer sought to uncover information about Rendar's involvement with the Alliance in order to sell it to the Empire. However, while Guri proved herself extremely tough in combat, Rendar and his companion were able to take out many of her thugs, forcing her to retreat.<ref name="LS" /> Rendar later attended the race but left during Chyler's test laps for another meeting with an Alliance operative. Walking along the track until the turn called [[The Sink Hole]], Rendar turned off and headed to a secluded location in the nearby swamp where he met with the Bothan [[Koth Melan]]. Melan handed Rendar a [[Datapad/Legends|datapad]], but then noticed that the Corellian was being followed by an Imperial. A firefight began, during which Melan was wounded and instructed Rendar to flee with the information, leaving himself to be captured.<ref name="DS" />

[[File:Bothan_Traitors.jpg|thumb|left|220px|Rendar fights alongside Koth Melan.]]
The final swoop race of the season was the [[Mos Espa Circuit|Mos Espa Race]] on Tatooine. Prince Xizor, who was looking to sponsor a racing team through his company, Xizor Transport Systems, threw a party before the race and invited Chyler, who needed one final victory to secure the championship. Rendar and his associate accompanied her to the event. After the party the trio stopped by a cantina in [[Mos Espa/Legends|Mos Espa]], where Rendar met with Rebel agent [[Luke Skywalker/Legends|Luke Skywalker]] and handed Melan's datapad over to him. However, the meeting was interrupted when Xizor and Guri entered the room. The [[Falleen/Legends|Falleen]] ordered his Human replica droid to take the datapad and kill the group. The resulting fight spilled out into the streets of Mos Espa, where Skywalker used his [[Lightsaber/Legends|lightsaber]] to protect Rendar and his companion from any blaster bolts. Xizor eventually chose to retreat without the datapad, promising to expose all information about Rendar, and his involvement with Skywalker, to the Emperor.<ref name="LS" />

====The Battle of Hoth====
{{Quote|Pretty good? I slept through most of that battle, kid. I could have stayed and knocked those walkers over all day without raising my heartbeat, if I hadn't had an appointment to pick up paying cargo elsewhere.|Dash Rendar|<ref name="SotE-N" />}}
The Rebels soon trusted Rendar enough that they shared with him the location of [[Echo Base/Legends|Echo Base]], the Alliance headquarters located in the [[Hoth system/Legends|Hoth system]].<ref name="CSWE" /> In [[3 ABY/Legends|3 ABY]],<ref name="NEC">''[[The New Essential Chronology]]''</ref> Rendar agreed to deliver supplies to [[Hoth/Legends|Hoth]]&mdash;in addition to the usual food supplies,<ref name="NEGTC" /> Rendar's cargo also included assault blasters to be delivered to Princess [[Leia Organa Solo/Legends|Leia Organa]].<ref name="SotE-PC">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Shadows of the Empire'' video game]] ([[Wikipedia:Personal computer|PC]] version)</ref>

Rendar and Leebo took the ''Outrider'' to the system and were allowed to dock in Echo Base's hangar,<ref name="SotE-VG">[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|''Shadows of the Empire'' video game]]</ref> where Rendar was surprised to run into Han Solo, who had become involved with the Rebellion since their last meeting. However, their reunion was cut short&mdash;[[Death Squadron/Legends|Imperial forces]] under the command of [[Sith Lord/Legends|Sith Lord]] [[Anakin Skywalker/Legends|Darth Vader]] had entered the Hoth system and were moving to [[Battle of Hoth/Legends|attack]] Echo Base.<ref name="SotE-N64" /> Unable to resist the battle,<ref name="FF25" /> and since he was still being paid,<ref name="SotES" /> Rendar decided to help delay the Imperial advance while the Rebels evacuated. He instructed Leebo to load their cargo into the evacuating [[GR-75 medium transport/Legends|transports]] and to retrieve their payment while he took an unused [[Snowspeeder/Legends|snowspeeder]] into combat against the advancing [[Imperial Army/Legends|Imperial ground forces]].<ref name="SotE-PC" /> On Solo's recommendation, Commander Skywalker agreed to let Rendar join [[Rogue Squadron/Legends|Rogue Squadron]] for the upcoming battle.<ref name="SotE-N64" />

[[File:Rendar_Snowspeeder.jpg|thumb|right|300px|Rendar flies a snowspeeder in the Battle of Hoth.]]
Rogue [[Squadron/Legends|Squadron]] engaged [[Viper probe droid/Legends|Viper probe droids]], [[All Terrain Scout Transport/Legends|All Terrain Scout Transports]] and [[All Terrain Armored Transport/Legends|All Terrain Armored Transports]],<ref name="SotE-VG" /> with Rendar, flying under the [[Callsign/Legends|call sign]] [[Rogue Twelve]], destroying one of the AT-AT [[Walker/Legends|walkers]], despite not having a gunner assigned to his snowspeeder.<ref name="TEGW">''[[The Essential Guide to Warfare]]''</ref> Despite Rogue Squadron's best efforts, however, the Imperials eventually destroyed Echo Base's [[Deflector shield generator/Legends|deflector shield generator]] and the Rebels were forced to withdraw.<ref name="SotE-VG" /> Rendar returned to Echo Base, calling ahead to instruct Leebo to have the ''Outrider'' ready to leave,<ref name="SotE-PC" /> but by the time he arrived, Imperial [[Cold assault stormtrooper|snowtroopers]] had overrun the facility and destroyed the [[Power generator/Legends|main generators]]. Leebo contacted Rendar to warn him that the hangar doors could not be opened to allow the ''Outrider'' to leave until power was restored. Fighting his way through both the Imperial forces and several wild [[Wampa/Legends|wampas]] that had entered the base, Rendar proceeded to the base's lower level and activated the emergency generators, restoring power to the hangar door. As he made his way back to the ''Outrider'', Rendar found his way blocked by an AT-ST. Fighting his way past the Imperial walker, Rendar returned to the ''Outrider'' to find the ship had already been boarded by Imperials. After killing the intruders, Rendar took the ''Outrider'' through the now-open hangar door and away from the planet. However, the ship did not get far before one of the orbiting Star Destroyers launched [[TIE/ln space superiority starfighter/Legends|TIE fighters]] and [[TIE/sa tactical bomber/Legends|TIE bombers]] to intercept. Unable to jump to hyperspace until they were clear of the [[Hoth asteroid field/Legends|Hoth asteroid field]], Leebo took control of the ''Outrider'', leading it through the [[Asteroid/Legends|asteroid]] belt while Rendar used the ship's gun turret to fend off the pursuing [[TIE series/Legends|TIEs]]. After clearing the asteroids, the ''Outrider'' jumped to safety<ref name="SotE-VG" /> and Rendar rejoined the Rebels.<ref name="CSWE" />

====The search for Solo====
{{Quote|You just left them there?''"<br />"''Hey, kid, I was paid to show them where ''Slave I'' was. I showed them. My job was done. If they'd wanted me to do anything else, they should have contracted for it up front.''"<br />"''If anything happens to them&mdash;''"<br />"''What, kid? You gonna shoot me? I didn't make them go there. I was hired as a guide, so I guided, end of story.|Luke Skywalker and Dash Rendar, following the Battle of Gall|<ref name="SotE-N" />}}
Shortly after the Battle of Hoth, Solo and Organa traveled to [[Cloud City/Legends|Cloud City]], a [[Mining/Legends|mining]] colony on [[Bespin/Legends|Bespin]] operated by Lando Calrissian. There, Solo was [[Occupation of Bespin|captured]] by the bounty hunter [[Boba Fett/Legends|Boba Fett]], who planned to collect a bounty on the smuggler by turning him over to the crime lord [[Jabba Desilijic Tiure/Legends|Jabba]] the Hutt. Solo was [[Carbon-freezing/Legends|frozen]] in [[Carbonite/Legends|carbonite]] for the journey to [[Jabba's Palace/Legends|Jabba's Palace]] on Tatooine.<ref name="ESB">{{Film|V}}</ref> Rendar learned that Organa was willing to pay well for help in locating Fett and rescuing Solo<ref name="SotES" /> and agreed to take the job as a favor to Calrissian,<ref name="NEGTC" /> who was already working with the Princess.<ref name="SotES" />

[[File:RendarsWrath_.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Dash Rendar confronts IG-88D.]]
In 3.5 ABY,<ref name="NEC" /> Rendar discovered that Fett had recently been involved in a [[Starfighter combat/Legends|dogfight]] with the bounty hunter droid [[IG-88D/Legends|IG-88D]], who had traveled to the junkyard world of [[Ord Mantell/Legends|Ord Mantell]] to scavenge for spare parts to repair his [[IG-2000/Legends|ship]]. Betting that IG-88D knew where Fett had gone following the fight, Rendar [[Mission to Ord Mantell (Dash Rendar)|followed]] the droid to Ord Mantell. Leebo used the ''Outrider''{{'s}} scanners to determine IG-88D's exact location, in a [[Junk Heap|salvage plant]] at the far end of the [[Scraplands/Legends|junkyard]] from their landing spot. Leebo informed Rendar that a [[Hovertrain/Legends|hovertrain]] led straight to the salvage plant's loading door. Boarding the nearest hovertrain, Rendar moved from train car to train car, fighting train guards and automated defenses along the way, until the tracks parallel to those of the train that lead to his destination. As the two trains moved alongside each other, Rendar leaped across the gap and made his way to the front of the new train. The salvage plant's loading door was closed but, once Rendar reached the engine car, Leebo was able to remotely disable the hovertrain's auto-brakes, causing the train to crash straight through the door. Inside, he was confronted by IG-88D, who revealed that he had indeed tracked Fett to the [[Zhar system]]. Unwilling to let Rendar stop him from taking Solo from Fett, the droid opened fire. Rendar fought back and was able to defeat the bounty hunter.<ref name="SotE-VG" />

Rendar reported his findings to Calrissian<ref name="SotE-N" /> and headed to the Imperial [[Imperial Enclave|moon base]] on [[Gall/Legends|Gall]] in the Zhar system to confirm Fett's location. Landing the ''Outrider'' safely out of sight in [[Smuggler's Canyon|Smuggler's Gorge]], Rendar left Leebo to watch the ship and proceeded on foot to the base's observation tower, hoping to access the central computer and find which hangar bay contained Fett. Making his way along the cliffside, Rendar encountered several Imperial patrols before reaching the entrance to the base itself. Rendar fought his way through the base until he reached the observation tower and accessed the computer, learning that Fett was docked in the second tower, on the other side of the nearby canyon. Taking a [[Jetpack/Legends|jetpack]] from the observation tower, Rendar crossed to another section of the Imperial base. As he continued to move through the base, Rendar came upon a large hangar containing an AT-ST. Using his jetpack to dodge its laser blasts, Rendar fired on the walker and eventually succeeded in felling it. A nearby switch provided access to the facility's ventilation system, which Rendar followed until it led him back outside near a waiting [[Hoversled/Legends|hoversled]]. Taking the hoversled to yet another section of the base, Rendar finally reached the landing pad where Fett's ship, [[Slave I/Legends|''Slave I'']], was docked. Fett opened fire upon seeing Rendar, but the smuggler fought back and Fett eventually fled into his ship. ''Slave I'' took off and Fett tried to use its weapons against Rendar, but the smuggler was able to damage the ship, leaving Fett stuck on Gall.<ref name="SotE-VG" />

[[File:GrandTrench-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Rendar leads the ''Millennium Falcon'' to Boba Fett.]]
Having confirmed that Fett was on Gall, Rendar placed a coded HoloNet call to Calrissian, who arranged to meet him in the Zhar system. Organa arranged for Rogue Squadron to assist in an attempted [[Battle of Gall|rescue]] and the Rogues established a [[Rebel base (Kile)|temporary base]] on the nearby moon [[Kile]]. Rendar was waiting at Rogue Squadron's base when Calrissian, Organa, and Chewbacca arrived aboard Solo's ''Millennium Falcon'', along with Skywalker in his [[T-65 X-wing starfighter/Legends|T-65 X-wing starfighter]]. [[Rogue Leader/Legends|Rogue Leader]] [[Wedge Antilles/Legends|Wedge Antilles]] briefed the new arrivals on the layout of the Imperial base and the expected opposition&mdash;two Star Destroyers, each with a [[Fighter wing/Legends|wing]] of starfighters. Skywalker proposed that he and Rogue Squadron attack, drawing off the defending TIE fighters, while Rendar led the ''Millennium Falcon'' and its crew to Fett's ship to retrieve Solo. Despite the risks, the group agreed to Skywalker's plan.<ref name="SotE-N" />

In order to avoid Imperial sensors, the ''Outrider'' and the ''Millennium Falcon'' were required to fly low. Rendar led the way, keeping the ''Outrider'' a few meters above tree level and eventually led them into the [[Grand Trench]] to avoid a long-range sensor post. Lifting out of the canyon after passing the sensor station, Rendar led the group toward the [[Shipyard/Legends|shipyard]] where Fett was. Less than a [[Standard minute/Legends|minute]] away from the target, however, Rendar bid them farewell and put the ''Outrider'' in a climb straight out of the [[Atmosphere/Legends|atmosphere]] before returning to the makeshift base on Kile. He arrived shortly after Rogue Squadron returned, having been forced to withdraw in the face of greatly superior numbers, and was met by Skywalker and Antilles. Although Skywalker was angry that Rendar had abandoned his friends, Rendar maintained that he had only been paid to lead them to Fett and that his work was complete. Before long, the ''Millennium Falcon'' too returned to Kile, having been unable to prevent Fett's escape with the frozen Solo.<ref name="SotE-N" />

====The secret plans====
{{Quote|Hey, lighten up, Dash. Things get heavy in the middle of a battle. Anybody can miss&mdash;''"<br />"''Not me! I don't miss. I should have clipped that missile! Bothans died because I missed, you understand?|Lando Calrissian and Dash Rendar, after the raid on the ''Suprosa''|<ref name="SotE-N" />}}
[[File:Rendar-Swoop.jpg|thumb|left|300px|Rendar rides a swoop to rescue Luke Skywalker.]]
Knowing that Fett would eventually deliver Solo to Jabba on Tatooine, Skywalker returned to his desert homeworld to wait for the bounty hunter to arrive. Following a recent attempt on Skywalker's life, Organa was concerned for his safety and hired Rendar to watch over him while she attempted to uncover who was behind the failed assassination attempt. Rendar followed Skywalker to Tatooine and, per Organa's instructions, kept a discreet distance,<ref name="SotE-N" /> watching for signs of trouble at one of his regular cantinas in Mos Eisley.<ref name="SotE-VG" /> While in Mos Eisley, Rendar overheard a [[Gizz's Gang|swoop gang]] discussing their plans to kill Skywalker on Jabba's orders. Taking a swoop of his own, Rendar followed the [[Swoop gang/Legends|gang]] as they headed to the deceased [[Jedi Master/Legends|Jedi Master]] [[Obi-Wan Kenobi/Legends|Obi-Wan Kenobi's]] [[Ben Kenobi's home/Legends|hut]] in the [[Dune Sea/Legends|Dune Sea]], which was serving as Skywalker's temporary residence. The gang soon reached Skywalker but he was able to take out one of the riders and flee aboard the man's swoop toward [[Beggar's Canyon/Legends|Beggar's Canyon]]. By the time Rendar arrived, Skywalker had almost halved his pursuers, but was still heavily outnumbered and running out of options. Dropping his swoop into the canyon, Rendar opened fire on the gang as he fell, causing them to scatter and flee.<ref name="SotE-N" />

After explaining his presence, Rendar returned with Skywalker to Kenobi's hut. The pair were discussing how to react to the attack on Skywalker when the Rebel's [[Astromech droid/Legends|astromech droid]], [[R2-D2/Legends|R2-D2]], detected the approach of a [[Seeker AS-M12 message droid|message droid]]. Rendar and Skywalker went to investigate and discovered that the droid had a message to deliver to Organa from Koth Melan. The Bothan claimed to have vital information for the Alliance and requested that Organa meet with him as soon as possible on his homeworld of [[Bothawui/Legends|Bothawui]]. In her absence, Skywalker decided to go to Bothawui to meet Melan and Rendar chose to accompany him in the interests of protecting his fee.<ref name="SotE-N" />

The two pilots brought their respective ships out of hyperspace in the [[Both system]] and managed to sneak into Bothawui past a nearby Imperial patrol. After landing, they caught a [[pubtrans flitter]] from the port into the city and made there way to the [[Intergalactic Trade Mission]] where Melan was expecting Organa. Rendar bribed the building's guard to let them pass and the pair proceeded to Melan's office on the sixteenth floor. When Melan's protocol droid, [[R0-4]], refused to let them in without an appointment, Rendar pulled his blaster. The droid reluctantly allowed them to enter Melan's office but the Bothan welcomed the pair and accepted them as Organa's representatives. The Bothans had learned of a new Imperial military construction project, which unbeknownst to them was a [[Death Star II/Legends|second Death Star]] [[Battle station/Legends|battle station]]. In order to uncover the exact nature of the project, Melan explained that they were planning to capture a secured [[Suprosa supercomputer|supercomputer]] containing the [[Death Star II plans|plans]], which was being transported from Coruscant to Bothawui aboard the ''[[Suprosa]]'', a [[MB-C1 medium transport|Mobquet medium transport]] masquerading as a fertilizer freighter. Though Melan had put together a Bothan team for the mission, he wanted Skywalker and Rendar to lead the [[Raid on the Suprosa|attack]]. Rendar was reluctant to get involved but agreed after Skywalker suggested that the Alliance may be willing to reward him for the supercomputer's capture.<ref name="SotE-N" />

[[File:Rendar-Suprosa.jpg|thumb|right|250px|Rendar fights stormtroopers aboard the ''Suprosa''.]]
Rendar and Skywalker traveled with Melan to a hidden base outside the city where they were introduced to the [[Blue Squadron (Bothan)|squadron]] of Bothan pilots he had assembled. When the Bothans learned of the ''Suprosa''{{'s}} route three days later, the group headed out, with Rendar carrying Melan's boarding party aboard the ''Outrider''. The ''Suprosa'' arrived as expected and Skywalker ordered its captain to surrender. When his request was refused, Skywalker ordered the Bothan [[BTL-S3 Y-wing starfighter/Legends|Y-wings]] to target the ship's engines and disable it. However, the ''Suprosa''{{'s}} weapons had been greatly upgraded and it opened fire, destroying one of the Y-wings and causing Skywalker to break his squadron off to regroup. As they pulled back, the freighter fired a [[Missile/Legends|missile]] at a group of four Bothan Y-wings. Seeing the threat, Rendar attempted to shoot down the missile. When he failed to stop it, the missile destroyed all four Y-wings, killing eight Bothans. Rendar, believing he had missed, blamed himself for their deaths; in truth, the [[Warhead/Legends|warhead]] had been a [[diamond boron missile]] and his shots had been unable to penetrate its armor. Despite their losses, the Rebels were soon able to disable the freighter and Rendar took the ''Outrider'' in to conduct the boarding operation.<ref name="SotE-N" /> Rendar docked the ''Outrider'' with the ''Suprosa'' and, putting his apparent failure behind him, boarded it personally to look for the supercomputer. Following Leebo's directions, Rendar worked his way through the ship toward the main cargo hangar where the supercomputer was located, encountering heavy resistance from the ''Suprosa''{{'s}} crew along the way. Upon reaching the cargo hangar, Rendar was attacked by a [[Imperial loader droid|loader droid]], but was able to destroy the droid and locate the supercomputer. After Rendar disabled the hangar [[Force field/Legends|force field]], Leebo brought the ''Outrider'' into the hangar to collect the smuggler and the supercomputer.<ref name="SotE-VG" />

Skywalker planned to accompany Melan to [[Kothlis/Legends|Kothlis]], where the Bothans could retrieve the data held on the supercomputer. Rendar, however, was still blaming himself for his failure to save the Bothans and Skywalker decided not to take him along, instead telling the smuggler to find Organa and tell her about the secret plans. As instructed, Rendar headed to Rodia, where he was met by Organa and Calrissian. After informing them about recent events, Rendar returned with them to the [[Flip of the Credit|casino]] where they were staying.<ref name="SotE-N" />

Organa hoped to enlist the help of Black Sun in tracking down whoever was responsible for the attempt on Skywalker's life and had already met once with Guri, acting as Xizor's representative. Having become suspicious that Guri was not as she seemed, Organa decided to take precautions and arranged for Rendar, Calrissian, and Chewbacca to act as her backup during the second meeting. With Rendar and Calrissian hidden in the suite's bedroom, and Chewbacca waiting in the corridor outside, Organa met once more with Guri. The droid, however, had instructions from Xizor to bring Organa back to him on Coruscant and, eventually tiring of the discussion with Organa, attempted to take her by force. On Organa's signal, Rendar and the others emerged, aiming their blasters at Guri. After the Human replica droid was restrained, the group discussed their next move. Despite Rendar and Calrissian's concerns, Organa agreed to go with Guri to Coruscant to seek assistance directly from Xizor. Though Chewbacca was to accompany her on the journey, Organa was unwilling to risk more lives than necessary and instructed Rendar and Calrissian to remain on Rodia and wait for Skywalker. However, Calrissian was not willing to simply sit and wait and, after Rendar provided him with Skywalker's location on Kothlis, he set off to rendezvous with his friend.<ref name="SotE-N" />

====Showdown with Xizor====
{{Dialogue|Luke Skywalker|There are six of them.|Lando Calrissian|Six? To guard a sewage plant?|Dash Rendar|So what? That's only one and a half each. How long does it take for you to pull a trigger, Calrissian?|attr=Luke Skywalker, Lando Calrissian, and Dash Rendar|src=<ref name="SotE-N" />}}
[[File:RendarSavesTheDay-SOTETC.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Rendar on Coruscant]]
Before long, Organa discovered who was behind the attempts on Skywalker's life&mdash;Xizor had learned that Skywalker was the son of his rival, the [[Dark Lord of the Sith/Legends|Dark Lord of the Sith]] [[Darth/Legends|Darth]] Vader and had dispatched his agents to kill the young Jedi. Though Chewbacca was able to escape from [[Xizor's Palace]] on Coruscant, Organa was being held captive by the [[Dark Prince]] and the Wookiee contacted Rendar to seek help from him and Calrissian. Wanting to make amends for his failure against the ''Suprosa'', Rendar left Chewbacca's message for Calrissian and departed for Coruscant. After arriving in the [[Coruscant system/Legends|Coruscant system]], the smuggler used the sensor shadow of a freighter to sneak past the Imperial authorities and land on the planet. Hoping to find a way to reach Organa, the smuggler made his way to a [[Spero's plant shop|plant shop]] in the area known as the [[Southern Underground/Legends|Southern Underground]], which was owned by the [[Master Gardener]] [[Spero]], a [[Ho'Din/Legends|Ho'Din]] with connections in the criminal underworld. Skywalker and Calrissian had also traveled to Coruscant upon receiving Chewbacca's message and Rendar arrived at the shop to find the three Rebels trapped inside as it came under attack by four armed men. Catching the attackers by surprise, Rendar opened fire and quickly eliminated them before leading the Rebels to a nearby [[Unidentified Southern Underground hotel|hotel]] to plan their next move.<ref name="SotE-N" />

Rendar suggested the group enter Xizor's Palace through the network of [[Sewers of Coruscant|sewage tunnels]] under the [[Galactic City/Legends|city]]. When the others agreed, he set up a meeting with [[Benedict Vidkun]], an [[Engineer/Legends|engineer]] with access to the sewers who was prepared to show them the way for the right price. A locked gate prevented access to the drain leading from Xizor's Palace from the main sewer tunnel, with a force field located in the smaller tunnel and finally another gate where the tunnel entered the palace. Vidkun's contacts could provide access to all three, leaving only the guards inside the palace entrance for Rendar and the Rebels to deal with. Though Rendar and the Rebels did not entirely trust Vidkun, they agreed to his price but insisted that he stay with them until they were ready to depart so as to prevent him from turning them in.<ref name="SotE-N" />

[[File:Rendar_shoots_Vidkun.jpg|thumb|right|260px|Rendar shoots Benedict Vidkun.]]
When they were ready, the group followed Vidkun into the main sewer tunnel and began working their way toward the palace. Along the way, a [[Dianoga/Legends|dianoga]] emerged from the sludge and attacked Skywalker. Rendar shouted a warning and drew his blaster, but Skywalker told him to hold his fire and instead dispatched the creature with his lightsaber. The group continued on, with Vidkun unlocking the first gate and deactivating the force field as they went. When they reached the final gate, Vidkun gave Calrissian the necessary keycard and turned to leave. Rendar blocked his path and insisted that he remain with the group until they were safely inside the palace, prompting the engineer to pull a small blaster from his coverall and begin firing at the group. His first shot went wide but the second grazed Rendar's hip. Before Vidkun could get off a third shot, Rendar produced his own blaster and shot the man in the head. After Rendar applied a surgical dressing to his wound, he and the others continued to the palace.<ref name="SotE-N" />

Finally reaching the end of the tunnel, the group spotted six guards playing a card game in the room beyond the exit. Rendar was confident that they could take out the guards but Skywalker hoped to avoid killing them. He instructed Rendar to open the hatch, then follow him, Chewbacca and Calrissian into the room. Rendar reluctantly agreed, but as Skywalker and Chewbacca emerged and instructed the guards not to move, the sewage-soaked Wookiee slipped and fell, knocking Calrissian over as he followed them through. The mishap gave the guards enough time to draw their weapons and open fire. Skywalker blocked the first shots with his lightsaber and Rendar emerged from the tunnel shooting, killing two of the guards. The two downed Rebels righted themselves and before long all six guards were dead, but not before one had managed to call for help.<ref name="SotE-N" />

The group began to work their way to where Organa was being held, encountering more guards along the way. They eventually ran into Organa, who had managed to escape from her room. Having located the princess, they headed up toward a landing pad where the droids R2-D2 and [[C-3PO/Legends|C-3PO]] would be waiting with the ''Millennium Falcon''. Upon reaching level twenty, however, they ran into a group of guards led by Guri and Xizor, who was personally leading the search for the intruders. Realizing they were outnumbered, Rendar suggested taking cover in a room off the main corridor. With no other way to escape, Skywalker activated the deadman's switch on a [[Thermal detonator/Legends|thermal detonator]] and moved back into the corridor to confront Xizor. Recognizing the device, the Falleen crime lord ordered his troops to cease fire and a standoff developed. Calrissian broke the stalemate by activating the five-minute timer on another detonator and placing it in a nearby [[Garbage pit|garbage chute]]. As Xizor's guards broke and fled in panic, Rendar and the others took the opportunity to slip away, taking a turbolift to the landing pad on level fifty.<ref name="SotE-N" />

[[File:Rendar-BattleOverCoruscant.jpg|thumb|left|260px|Rendar and Leebo during the Battle over Coruscant]]
They finally reached the landing pad moments before the ''Millennium Falcon'' came into view, approaching in an erratic manner under the control of its inexperienced droid pilots. After a shaky landing, the droids opened the ship's hatch and Rendar's group hurried aboard. Rendar reached the [[Cockpit/Legends|cockpit]] first and shoved C-3PO out of the pilot's seat before flying the ship to safety. Moments later, the thermal detonator exploded and [[Destruction of Xizor's Palace|destroyed]] Xizor's Palace.<ref name="SotE-N" />

Once safely away from the palace, Rendar signaled Leebo and instructed the droid to bring the ''Outrider'' into orbit to rendezvous with the ''Millennium Falcon''. After Leebo arrived, Rendar borrowed a [[Environment suit/Legends|vac suit]] from the ''Falcon'' and made the short trip back to his ship. However, as the two ships prepared to go their own ways, they were [[Battle over Coruscant|attacked]] by a group of Black Sun vessels. The two freighters were heavily outnumbered but were soon reinforced by Rogue Squadron,<ref name="SotE-N" /> who had been waiting at the edge of the Coruscant system following an earlier message from Leebo.<ref name="LG">{{WEGCite|story=Let's Go!|book=Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook}}</ref> However, Xizor's forces still had a numerical advantage and the battle was slowly turning against the Rebels until the arrival of Imperial forces led by Darth Vader on the [[Super Star Destroyer/Legends|Super Star Destroyer]] [[Executor/Legends|''Executor'']]. Vader had learned of Xizor's attempts to kill Skywalker and dispatched his TIE fighters to intercept Xizor's forces while the ''Executor'' turned its weapons on Xizor's [[Skyhook/Legends|skyhook]], ''[[Falleen's Fist]]'', to where the Dark Prince had fled after the destruction of his palace.<ref name="SotE-N" />

When the skyhook was destroyed, Rendar spotted a way out of the battle through the debris and led the way to safety.<ref name="SotE-N" /> However, despite helping to rescue Organa, Rendar still had no intention of formally siding with the Alliance, and was eager to avoid retribution from Black Sun for his part in Xizor's downfall.<ref name="SotE-PC" /> He saw his opportunity to escape as a large chunk of debris drifted into the path of the ''Outrider''. At the very last moment before colliding, Rendar took the ''Outrider'' into hyperspace, leaving those aboard the ''Millennium Falcon'' to believe he had been killed on impact.<ref name="FF25" />

===Later life and career===
{{Quote|Captain, I do not understand. Why do you not want Commander Skywalker and the others to know that we survived and made the jump to hyperspace?''"<br />"''Well, as much fun as that was, I don't see us joining the ranks of that crazy Rebellion. Too dangerous, and too much money to be made elsewhere, my friend. On top of that, someone from Black Sun will take Xizor's place, and when that happens, you can bet your servo-motors they'll send every thug in the galaxy after us. But if everyone thinks we're dead, who's gonna be looking? Besides, it's good to be remembered as a martyr without actually having to be dead, wouldn't you say?|Leebo and Dash Rendar|<ref name="SotE-VG" />}}
[[File:Dash_rendar_sotee.jpg|thumb|right|210px|Rendar on Hurd's Moon]]
The rumors of his death allowed Rendar to lay low for some time.<ref name="FF25" /> At some point when the Galactic Civil War was ongoing, smuggler [[Platt Okeefe/Legends|Platt Okeefe]] mentioned Rendar when writing the [[Smuggler's Handbook/Legends|''Smuggler's Handbook'']] document, noting Rendar as a rival smuggler who had taken Solo's place as the King of Brash.<ref name="Platt's Smugglers Guide">''[[Platt's Smugglers Guide]]''</ref> In the years following his apparent death, there were sporadic sightings of Rendar and the ''Outrider'', none of which were confirmed by the Rebel Alliance's successor, the [[New Republic/Legends|New Republic]]. Although some believed he had managed to use the ship's escape pod to flee before its destruction, those closest to Rendar maintained that he would never have abandoned the ''Outrider''.<ref name="NEGVV">''[[The New Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''</ref>

In 4 ABY,<ref name="4ABY">''[[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire: Evolution]]'' takes place four years after [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], which ''[[The New Essential Chronology]]'' places in [[0 ABY/Legends|0 ABY]].</ref> Rendar was on [[Hurd's Moon]] in the [[Mid Rim/Legends|Mid Rim]] when Guri traveled to the world to seek the assistance of [[Massad Thrumble]], one of her original designers, in purging her assassin programming. The procedure was a success and Guri later visited a local cantina where Rendar was waiting. Rendar waved the droid over to his table and formally introduced himself before offering to buy her a drink.<ref name="SotE:E">[[Shadows of the Empire: Evolution 5|''Shadows of the Empire: Evolution'' 5]]</ref> The two eventually formed a mercenary team,<ref name="TDFS" /> and were recruited by [[Admiral/Legends|Admiral]] [[Gial Ackbar/Legends|Gial Ackbar]] of the New Republic to help place a [[Spy/Legends|spy]] on the [[Tof/Legends|Tof]] fortress world of [[Saijo/Legends|Saijo]],<ref name="TFW">{{Hyperspace|url=fans/hyperspace/source/nagai11202009/index.html|text=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs|int=The Forgotten War: The Nagai and the Tofs}}</ref> teaming up with New Republic agents [[Kyle Katarn]] and [[Bey]] for the [[Battle of Saijo|mission]].<ref name="TDFS" />

Rendar quickly saw the potential to create new Human replica droids based on Guri's technology. The droid agreed to allow herself to be used as a template and served as his partner during the research and development phase.<ref name="ODT">{{InsiderCite|75|Or Die Trying}}</ref> Adapting [[Ssi-ruu]]k [[entechment]] technology, Rendar and Guri also discovered that it was possible to store a Human's mind in an HRD's computer. They established [[Onadax Droid Technologies]],<ref name="CSWE" /> a company based on [[Onadax]]<ref name="CSWE-ODT">{{CSWECite|II|412|Onadax Droid Technologies}}</ref> in the [[Minos Cluster/Legends|Minos Cluster]],<ref name="CSWE-Onadax">{{CSWECite|II|412|Onadax}}</ref> and tested their new technology by creating a [[Stanton Rendar (droid)|Human replica droid]] of Rendar's own brother, Stanton.<ref name="CSWE" /> Rendar and Guri went their separate ways sometime after this,<ref name="ODT" /> leaving the replica of Stanton to serve as head of ODT.<ref name="CSWE" /> ''[[The Essential Chronology]]'', a document written in [[25 ABY/Legends|25 ABY]], mentioned Rendar's involvement in the raid on the ''Suprosa''.<ref name="TEC">[[The Essential Chronology (real-world book)|''The Essential Chronology'']]</ref> By the time ODT's Onadax facility was infiltrated by [[Jedi Knight/Legends|Jedi Knight]] [[Jaina Solo Fel|Jaina Solo]] during an investigation into the new HRDs<ref name="ODT" /> in [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]],<ref name="28ABY">"[[Or Die Trying]]" dates itself between the novels ''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic II: Refugee]]'' and ''[[The New Jedi Order: Force Heretic III: Reunion]]'', which take place in [[28 ABY/Legends|28 ABY]] according to ''[[The Essential Reader's Companion]]''.</ref> Rendar was still widely believed to be dead.<ref name="ODT" /> However, reports of sightings continued throughout the [[Yuuzhan Vong War]], during which Rendar was seen sabotaging the efforts of the [[Yuuzhan Vong]] collaborators in the [[Peace Brigade]].<ref name="NEGTC" /> [[36 ABY]]'s [[The New Essential Chronology (in-universe)|updated]] version of ''The Essential Chronology'' would repeat the information about Rendar's involvement in raiding the ''Suprosa''.<ref name="NEC" />

==Personality and traits==
{{Quote|Something to prove, I guess. I felt pretty bad after that disaster Luke and I went through. Not something I'm used to, making mistakes. But I figure, you crash your ship, you better climb into the next one you see and get it back in the air. Too much time goes by and you don't, you get afraid to fly. I screwed up, and I'm still not over that, but you can only sit and bubble in your own juices for so long. I work for money, but I figure I owe the Empire a little something. When Chewie called, I decided it was time to pay the Empire back.|Dash Rendar|<ref name="SotE-N" />}}
Tall and lean, with [[Color/Legends|red]] [[Hair/Legends|hair]], green eyes and pale skin, Rendar was considered attractive and was popular with both students and teachers alike during his time at the Imperial Academy.<ref name="FF25" /> The death of his brother changed Rendar, leaving him with a bitter resentment of both the Empire and Black Sun.<ref name="SG" /> He lost the clean-cut looks and well-spoken voice,<ref name="FF25" /> developing a more chiseled, muscular appearance<ref name="CSWE" /> with the lazy, insolent attitude common among smugglers,<ref name="SotES" /> and giving those he met the impression of a rugged, streetwise mercenary with a sharp wit.<ref name="FF25" /> Despite his outward appearance of nonchalance, Rendar was constantly aware of his surroundings and his hand rarely strayed far from his blaster.<ref name="Fear" /> These traits marked him as a survivor,<ref name="FF25" /> and he was even prepared to fake his own death to avoid retribution from Black Sun after his involvement in the death of Prince Xizor.<ref name="SotE-PC" />

[[File:DashRendar-NEGTC.png|thumb|left|180px|Dash Rendar]]
Rendar was a skilled pilot. While studying at the Imperial Academy, he frequently impressed both his fellow [[Cadet/Legends|cadets]] and his instructors<ref name="SotES" /> by executing maneuvers that pushed the ships he flew well beyond their usual limits. After leaving the Academy, it was not long before Rendar discovered that his piloting skills had the potential to serve him well as a smuggler.<ref name="Kenner">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Dash Rendar|link=soteKdash.asp}}</ref> Never short of confidence, Rendar frequently boasted that he was able to fly any ship and was equally good with a blaster.<ref name="SotES" /> Having always sought excitement,<ref name="FF25" /> he was more than willing to try any stunt, no matter how dangerous, to back up his claims. Some believed Rendar's arrogance and reckless attitude were simply to impress his peers; others thought that he was attempting to push himself and discover his own limits. While Rendar focused on his flying skills, he lacked the patience for the less glamorous aspects of smuggling, and preferred to delegate tasks such as conducting repairs and arranging meetings to Leebo.<ref name="SotES" /> The ''Outrider''{{'s}} advanced systems helped Rendar to stand out among his smuggling rivals.<ref name="FF25" /> With Rendar at the helm, the ''Outrider'' was a deadly opponent for any pilot,<ref name="Kenner" /> saving his life on several occasions and leading him to develop an emotional attachment to the ship.<ref name="EGVV" /> He became so accustomed to success that when his skills appeared to fail him during the attack on the ''Suprosa'', he was plunged into a deep depression and blamed himself for the loss of the Bothan pilots.<ref name="SotE-N" />

As a teenager, Rendar longed for independence and chose to train at the Imperial Academy rather than join the family business. This independent streak remained with him throughout his career and, despite his personal grudge against the Empire, he was not willing to trade in his independence to formally join the Rebel Alliance. The loss of his family also made him unwilling to form emotional bonds; he used his arrogant attitude to keep others from getting close to him and felt that he could only rely on himself.<ref name="FF25" /> Javul Charn was among the few individuals to whom Rendar became close. Rendar felt an instant attraction to Charn when he was hired to protect her and the two shared several intimate moments during her tour<ref name="SG" /> in 0 BBY.<ref name="ERC" /> Yet, even though Rendar cared about Charn and was determined to ensure her safety, he was unwilling to abandon his independence to join her after learning of her involvement with the Rebellion. Rendar was also close to his Nautolan co-pilot and navigator, Eaden Vrill. The two worked together for some time before joining Charn's tour and Rendar felt anger and loss after Vrill's death on Bannistar Station. Following Vrill's death,<ref name="SG" /> Rendar rarely traveled with anybody other than Leebo and the droid was one of few individuals he trusted.<ref name="FF56" /> Rendar maintained a competitive rivalry with his friends, Han Solo and Lando Calrissian, spending many hours attempting to outdo them with tales of his adventures<ref name="SotES" /> and often trading insults with both about their respective piloting skills.<ref name="SotE-N" /><ref name="SG" /> One such incident became physical when a drunken Solo threw a punch at Rendar.<ref name="SG" /> Upon acquiring the ''Outrider'', Rendar was eager to show it off to Solo and make the other smuggler jealous.<ref name="AtE" /> The two went on to race their ships, with Solo narrowly coming out on top on at least one occasion,<ref name="SotE-N64" /> but Rendar remained convinced that he had the faster ship.<ref name="BtMF6" /> When escorting Javul Charn, Rendar almost quit as her bodyguard rather than travel aboard Solo's ''Millennium Falcon''.<ref name="SG" />

Rendar was not one to waste his talents fighting for a cause and only took on work if he was well compensated. He always insisted on half of his payment up front and half when the job was completed. As long as he was getting paid, he was trustworthy and loyal,<ref name="SotES" /> willing and able to protect his cargo.<ref name="DS" /> When hired to locate the captive Han Solo, Rendar followed the terms of his employment exactly, leading Lando Calrissian and Leia Organa to the smuggler's location but departing before the fighting began.<ref name="SotE-N" /> He did not believe in doing work as a favor and made sure that he never had any debts for others to call on. Likewise, Rendar made sure that nobody ever owed him.<ref name="SotES" /> However, his mercenary attitude disguised a hidden noble streak.<ref name="CSWE" /> When Rendar felt that he had failed to protect the Bothan pilots, he voluntarily risked his life to rescue Organa from Xizor's Palace, hoping to make amends for his earlier failure.<ref name="SotE-N" />

==Equipment==
Rendar was usually seen wearing a blue and brown [[Jumpsuit/Legends|jumpsuit]]&mdash;typical attire for freighter captains at the time&mdash;along with a [[flexmetal]] [[Blast vest/Legends|blast vest]] with padded<ref name="SotES" /> [[19-96 Kinetic Absorption Panel]]<ref name="GoH">''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]''</ref> [[Pauldron/Legends|pauldrons]] that provided some protection during [[lightfight]]s and a pair of brown flight [[Glove/Legends|gloves]]. A [[PAC20 Visual Wrist Comm]] on his wrist provided him with a long range shielded single-channel link to Leebo, and he sometimes carried a small [[Comlink/Legends|comlink]] on his [[Utility belt/Legends|belt]] as an emergency back-up. His outfit was completed by a [[Heavy blaster pistol/Legends|heavy blaster pistol]], the model being a [[DL-44 heavy blaster pistol/Legends|DL-44 heavy blaster pistol]], slung low on his hip. Rendar sometimes carried additional equipment and weapons when required,<ref name="SotES" /> including [[Disruptor rifle/Legends|disrupters]], [[seeker missile]]s, [[Stunner/Legends|stunners]], [[Flamethrower/Legends|flamethrowers]], and [[Pulse cannon/Legends|pulse cannons]],<ref name="SotE-VG" /> but generally preferred to travel light.<ref name="SotES" />

===LE-BO2D9===
[[File:LE-BO2D9.png|thumb|right|240px|Leebo]]
{{Quote|Hey, Leebo, you rust bucket, get your gears meshing and meet me at the following coordinates.''"<br />"''My master is not in at the moment. Who is calling, please?''"<br />"''Very funny. Never buy a droid programmed by a failed comedian.|Dash Rendar and Leebo|<ref name="SotE-N" />}}
{{Main|LE-BO2D9/Legends}}
LE-BO2D9, nicknamed Leebo, was an early Cybot Galactica LE-series repair droid originally owned by the portmaster at [[Esseles/Legends|Esseles]] starport. After a freighter lifted off with Leebo still aboard, he became a shipboard mechanic, going through a series of owners, who each updated the droid with new skills.<ref name="LeeboDB">{{DB|droid|lebo2d9leebo|LE-BO2D9 (Leebo)}}</ref> He eventually ended up in service to Kood Gareeda, a Rodian comedian who gave Leebo personality programming<ref name="Insider128" /> and a quirky sense of humor.<ref name="LeeboDB" /> Leebo managed the comedian during a tour of the Outer Rim Territories before being sold to Rendar,<ref name="SotES" /> who modified the droid with enhanced repair and piloting skills, and a long range shielded comlink.<ref name="LeeboDB" /> Leebo became a faithful companion to Rendar, serving as his co-pilot and flying backup for Rendar when the smuggler got into trouble. The droid also took on much of the work Rendar lacked the patience for, such as arranging meetings with contacts, surveying smuggling markets and making repairs to the ''Outrider''.<ref name="SotES" />

===''Outrider''===
{{Quote|I owe the ''Outrider'' the best. She's brought me home when any other ship would have scattered me across space.|Dash Rendar|<ref name="NEGVV" />}}
{{Main|Outrider/Legends}}
[[File:Outrider_-_SWGTCG.jpg|thumb|right|220px|The ''Outrider'']]
The ''Outrider'' was a [[Corellian Engineering Corporation/Legends|Corellian Engineering Corporation]] YT-2400 light freighter originally intended as a medium-range cargo vessel.<ref name="NEGVV" /> Rendar acquired the ''Outrider'' while working for "Uncle" Vanya during his early career,<ref name="UA:SSWR" /> and had the ship heavily modified to suit his needs.<ref name="NEGVV" /> One of Rendar's first upgrades was replacing the original hyperdrive with a Class 0.75 SoroSuub Corporation [[Griffyn/Y2TG hyperdrive]], and he subsequently replaced the stock [[Sublight engine/Legends|sublight engines]] with three stolen military-grade [[KonGar Ship Works]] [[KGDefender ion engine]]s.<ref name="BtMF6" /> The weapons systems were augmented with two [[Dymek/Legends|Dymek]] [[Laser cannon/Legends|double laser cannons]],<ref name="NEGVV" /> modified for increased range and capable of being controlled remotely from the cockpit.<ref name="NEGVV" /> Rendar also fitted two [[Concussion missile launcher/Legends|concussion missile launchers]] for additional firepower.<ref name="BtMF6" />

Additional modifications included reinforced [[Titanium/Legends|titanium]] hull armor,<ref name="BtMF6" /> improved deflector shields, a sensor stealth system,<ref name="NEGVV" /> and a countermeasures package.<ref name="BtMF6" /> Most of the modifications were illegal and Rendar broke several laws every time he used the ship.<ref name="NEGVV" /> Nevertheless, the ''Outrider'' saved Rendar's life on numerous occasions and the smuggler formed an emotional attachment to the vessel.<ref name="EGVV" />

===''Outrunner''===
{{Quote|That ship's gotten me through some tough scrapes. I gotta return the favor.|Dash Rendar, on the ''Outrunner''|<ref name="Fear" />}}
{{Main|Outrunner}}
The ''Outrunner'' was purchased by Rendar as a second ship, using the profits from his early career as a freelancer.<ref name="NEGTC" /> The vessel was black and so streamlined that it reminded Zak Arranda of a missile about to be fired. The ship could be made ready to fly at short notice and was well armed, with multiple weapon turrets, including a turbolaser that could be extended from a hole in the hull, and forward warhead launchers.<ref name="Fear" />

==Behind the scenes==
{{Quote|We know ''[Rendar is]'' designed to be around while the swashbuckling Han is encased in carbonite, but we don't want Dash to be a carbonite copy of Mr. Solo. Our suggestion is that rather than thinking of him simply as a mercenary, Dash is more like a swaggery ''Top Gun''-style fighter pilot. A guy with real talent but a bit of a braggart and a blowhard, too. Luke doesn't like him, not only because of this in-your-face personality but also because of the natural competitiveness between these two pilots.|Bantam Spectra editor Tom Dupree's pre-manuscript note to Steve Perry|<ref name="Secrets">''[[The Secrets of Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire]]''</ref>}}
Dash Rendar was developed for the [[1996]] multimedia project [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|''Shadows of the Empire'']] and appeared in its [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (novel)|novel]], [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (comic series)|comic]] and [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (video game)|video game]] incarnations.<ref name="SotE-N" /><ref name="SotE-VG" /><ref name="SotE2">[[Shadows of the Empire 2|''Shadows of the Empire'' 2]]</ref> [[Star Wars Insider 28|''Star Wars Insider'' 28]] and [[Star Wars Galaxy Magazine 6|''Star Wars Galaxy Magazine'' 6]], both released in early 1996, were the first published sources to mention Rendar in articles previewing ''Shadows of the Empire'' and a [[Operator's Manual|preview]] of [[Bill Smith]]'s 1996 reference book, ''[[The Essential Guide to Vehicles and Vessels]]''.<ref name="Insider28">{{InsiderCite|28|Lucasfilm's Latest}}</ref><ref name="Galaxy6">{{GalaxyCite|6|Operator's Manual}}</ref> 

[[LucasArts]] made a small statue of Dash whose dimensions and proportions were scanned in order to develop further consistent designs. Rendar had a supporting role in the narrative of [[Steve Perry]]'s ''Shadows of the Empire'' comics and novel; however he was the protagonist of the ''Shadows of the Empire'' [[Star Wars video games|video game]] adaptation, as players controlled the mercenary through twelve separate missions loosely following the course of the ''Shadows'' storyline.<ref name="Secrets" />

{{Listen2|SOTE4.flac|"Beggar's Canyon Chase"|A theme for Dash Rendar briefly appears at the end of "Beggar's Canyon Chase."}}
As part of ''Shadows of the Empire'', composer [[Joel McNeely]] wrote a fifty-one-minute [[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)|orchestral score]]. The track "[[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)#Beggar.27s Canyon Chase|Beggar's Canyon Chase]]," depicting the swoop bike chase through Beggar's Canyon, ends with a brief statement of "[[Dash's theme]]" as he arrives to rescue Skywalker.<ref name="Soundtrack">[[Shadows of the Empire (soundtrack)|''Shadows of the Empire'' soundtrack]] album liner notes</ref>

[[Kenner Products|Kenner's]] [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|''Shadows of the Empire'' toy line]], released in 1996, included an action figure of Rendar. The Rendar figure included a blaster pistol and a heavy weapons pack.<ref name="Kenner" /> The ''Outrider'' was also released as a toy as part of this line.<ref name="KennerOutrider">{{KennerCite|set=Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire (toy line)|pack=Dash Rendar's ''Outrider''|link=soteKoutrider.asp}}</ref>

[[File:TomKyte.jpg|thumb|left|180px|Tom Kyte posing as Dash Rendar for a ''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' trading card reference photograph.]]
Rendar has subsequently made several appearances, including the [[1998]] [[Star Wars comic books|comic series]] [[Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire: Evolution|''Shadows of the Empire: Evolution'']] by Steve Perry,<ref name="SotE:E" /> the 1998 novels ''[[Rebel Dawn]]'' by [[A. C. Crispin]] and ''[[Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship]]'' by [[John Whitman]],<ref name="RD" /><ref name="Fear" /> the [[1999]] [[LucasArts]] [[Star Wars video games|video game]] ''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]'' and the [[2009]] ''[[Star Wars Galaxies Trading Card Game]]'' expansion ''[[The Shadow Syndicate]]''.<ref name="LS" /><ref name="DS" /><ref name="XWA">''[[Star Wars: X-Wing Alliance]]''</ref> Steve Perry has said that he would like to write a story about Rendar and Han Solo teaming up and is also interested in further exploring Rendar's collaboration with Guri. Perry and [[Michael Reaves]] pitched an idea to [[Del Rey]] and [[Lucasfilm]] for a story that would include Rendar, but no such project has been announced.<ref name="YS">{{WebCite|url=http://yildizsavaslari.com/inceleme/steveperry/index_eng.html|text=Steve Perry Interview|work=YildizSavaslari.com|archivedate=20111118211500}}</ref> Rendar, however, is the protagonist in the [[2011]] Del Rey novel ''[[Shadow Games]]'' by Reaves and [[Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff]], in which he does partner up with Han Solo.<ref name="SG" /> Rendar is also the protagonist in Reaves and Bohnhoff's 2011 [[Star Wars Insider 128|''Star Wars Insider'' 128]] short story "''[[And Leebo Makes Three]]''."<ref name="Insider128" />

In the [[1997]] [[The Star Wars Trilogy Special Edition|Special Edition]] of [[Star Wars: Episode IV A New Hope|''Star Wars'': Episode IV ''A New Hope'']], Rendar's ''Outrider'' can be seen taking off from Mos Eisley as Luke Skywalker's [[X-34 landspeeder/Legends|landspeeder]] enters the town.<ref name="OutriderDB">{{DB|starship|outrider|Outrider}}</ref> The [[2006]] [[Hyperspace: The Official Star Wars Fan Club|Hyperspace]] article ''[[Underworld Appendix: Swoops, Spice, and Wretched Rogues]]'' by [[Abel G. Peña]] and [[Ryan Kaufman (real person)|Ryan Kaufman]] introduced an explanation for Rendar's presence in the town, stating that he had been purchasing weapons and made his sudden departure after hearing that his brother was still alive.<ref name="UA:SSWR" />

Rendar was voiced by [[John Cygan]] in the PC version of ''Shadows of the Empire''.<ref name="SotE-PC" /> Cygan reprised the role in ''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]'', in which the character is available as a hero in the custom scenario editor.<ref name="GB">''[[Star Wars: Galactic Battlegrounds: Clone Campaigns]]''</ref> The [[1996 Topps Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|''Shadows of the Empire'' trading cards]], released by [[Topps]] in 1996, featured a series of paintings by artists [[Greg Hildebrandt|Greg]] and [[Tim Hildebrandt]]. Model [[Tom Kyte]] posed in costume as Rendar for photographs that were used as a reference for the Hildebrandts' paintings.<ref name="Galaxy9">{{GalaxyCite|9|Filling in the Shadows}}</ref>

Rendar is briefly mentioned in the non-[[canon]] [[2015]] video game ''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''. During the Hoth mission, one of the non-player characters in Echo Base can be heard saying "Glad K-3PO is here. He's got some great supplies. Cheaper then that smuggler guy was. Rendar, that was him. And his droid, Leebo, creeped me out too".<ref name="Infinity">''[[Disney Infinity 3.0]]''</ref> Rendar was one of five characters from the [[Star Wars Legends|''Star Wars'' Legends]] continuity added to the mobile game ''[[Star Wars: Galaxy of Heroes]]'' in [[2021]] to celebrate the fiftieth anniversary of Lucasfilm.<ref name="LF50">{{EA|subdomain=forums.galaxy-of-heroes.starwars|url=discussion/251416/lucasfilm-50th-anniversary-and-upcoming-legends-characters|text=Lucasfilm 50th Anniversary and Upcoming Legends Characters}}</ref>

===Genesis===
{{Quote|I thought it'd be fun to do someone who could contrast between Han and Lando. Someone very reckless, nasty, tough, slightly running to fat and a bit of a slob who could take insane amounts of punishment and keep going.|Kilian Plunkett, on his early Rendar sketches|<ref name="Secrets" />}}
In [[1994]], Lucasfilm began working on ''Shadows of the Empire'', a project that would cross several different formats and involve multiple licensees, including a [[Bantam Spectra]] novel, a [[Dark Horse Comics]] comic series and a LucasArts video game. Lucasfilm's [[Howard Roffman]] and [[Lucy Autrey Wilson|Lucy Wilson]] prepared a two-page outline of the basic premise for the project's story, which would be set between [[Star Wars: Episode V The Empire Strikes Back|''Star Wars'': Episode V ''The Empire Strikes Back'']] and [[Star Wars: Episode VI Return of the Jedi|''Star Wars'': Episode VI ''Return of the Jedi'']]. This initial outline included the idea of an assassin targeting Luke Skywalker and a bodyguard assigned to protect him. In a meeting between Lucasfilm and their licensees in [[November]] 1994 to develop an outline of the plot, Steve Perry proposed the character of Rendar, who it was decided should take on the bodyguard role. The LucasArts representatives liked the new character and soon made the decision to use him as the [[Wikipedia:Player character|player character]] in the video game.<ref name="Secrets" />

[[File:Rendar-Concept.jpg|thumb|Before settling with Rendar as a charismatic and flamboyant hero, at some point the designers experimented with different archetypes. This sketch for Dash Rendar by Kilian Plunkett reflects that early stage of conception, with a proposal to make Dash an asocial, gruff and unkempt underground character.]]
Perry envisioned Rendar as a dashing character who would fill the gap left by Han Solo's imprisonment in carbonite at the end of ''The Empire Strikes Back''. However, as the project moved forward, Dark Horse artist [[Kilian Plunkett]] developed some designs of the character that differed from Perry's initial idea. In Plunkett's sketches, Rendar was tough, wild-eyed, unshaven, disheveled, and starting toward overweight. Plunkett wanted to keep the character in the same vein as Solo, but to ensure that they were not too similar in appearance, a concern shared by Bantam editor [[Tom Dupree]]. On one of his early sketches, Plunkett noted that Rendar was the "character most likely to have 'mom' tattooed on his arm."<ref name="Secrets" />

Around the same time, concept artist [[Michael Butkus|Mike Butkus]] developed dozens of preliminary sketches of Rendar, showing variations in armor and clothing but sticking to a more clean cut appearance. Butkuss, who listens to music while he illustrates, explained that Rendar was designed while listening to [[Wikipedia:Elvis Presley|Elvis Presley]] and [[1960s]] [[Wikipedia:Rock and roll|rock 'n' roll]]. Butkus's designs were circulated to those working on the project and led to some disagreement over the appearance of the character. LucasArts lead artist and designer [[Jon Knoles]] had concerns about Butkus's sketches from a game design perspective, wanting to see his muscles toned down, his clothing less tight and his bushy hair replaced with something less "goofy." Knoles suggested either following Plunkett's ideas of a mean-looking character or making him have the appearance of a determined, angry young warrior. Knoles's own designs experimented with the character further, with variations on armor, helmets, a mustache, and a [[Wikipedia:Van dyke beard|Vandyke beard]].<ref name="Secrets" />

Lucy Wilson favored a young and heroic appearance for Rendar and Tom Dupree wanted the character to be a [[Wikipedia:Top Gun|Top Gun]]-style fighter pilot who would have a combination of talent and ego that led to a natural competitiveness with Skywalker. Over four or five months, Butkus and Knoles refined the designs, settling on a final design that was a middle ground between Butkus's clean-cut and Plunkett's rugged sketches. LucasArts produced a sculpture of this final design, which was scanned to provide dimensional information used in producing his computer model.<ref name="Secrets" />

As with his appearance, Rendar's backstory was also refined during the development of the project. An early biography of Rendar included in Knoles's Game Design Outline document, dated [[January 26]], [[1995]], describes Rendar as an enlisted pilot in the Imperial Academy who crashed a prototype Imperial fighter into a statue of Emperor Palpatine while conducting a careless maneuver during a ceremony for the Emperor on Coruscant. Rendar was called before the Emperor and made to watch as a [[Gladiator droid/Legends|gladiator droid]] executed his brother, an independent freighter pilot who was suspected of having Rebel sympathies. Rendar was subsequently sentenced to life on a [[Prison ship/Legends|dungeon ship]], but was freed during a Rebel raid on the prison. Inheriting the ''Outrider'' from his brother and filled with a desire to gain vengeance on the Empire, Rendar dedicated himself to the Rebel Alliance, but, while his skills were seen as invaluable, he gained a reputation for reckless tactics that put both himself and others at risk.<ref name="GDO">{{WebCite|url=http://www.wilmunder.com/Arics_World/Games_files/1995%2001%2026%20Shadows%20of%20the%20Empire.compressed.pdf|text=''Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire'' Game Design Outline|author=[[Jon Knoles]]|date=1995-01-26|work=[http://www.wilmunder.com/Arics_World Aric's World]|archivedate=20170701093530}}</ref>

The ''Shadows of the Empire'' game was one of the early Nintendo 64 titles and the new technology presented LucasArts with the opportunity to recreate scenes from the [[original trilogy]] in a way that had not previously been possible, specifically the Battle of Hoth, which had first appeared in ''The Empire Strikes Back''. To accommodate this, Rendar's biography was written to incorporate his involvement in the battle, which is depicted in the opening levels of the game.<ref name="Secrets" />

Steve Perry's original outline for ''Shadows of the Empire'' described Rendar escaping the climactic battle over Coruscant moments before Darth Vader's forces destroy Xizor's skyhook. It was later decided that the destruction of the ''Outrider'' would make a more dramatic ending for the novel, but this presented a problem for LucasArts, who were concerned about killing off the player character at the end of the game. One possible solution would have been to change the player character to Skywalker, but LucasArts wanted to explore a new character in the game. To accommodate the game, Rendar's death was left ambiguous in the novel<ref name="Secrets" /> and the game includes a final cutscene, shown only when completed on the harder difficulty settings, in which Rendar and Leebo discuss their last-minute escape.<ref name="SotE-VG" /> Rendar's survival was also revealed in ''Shadows of the Empire: Evolution'' and has been mentioned in several reference sources, including ''[[The Official Star Wars Fact File 25]]'', ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'', and ''The Complete Star Wars Encyclopedia''.<ref name="NEGTC" /><ref name="CSWE" /><ref name="FF25" /><ref name="SotE:E" />

===Inconsistencies===
{{Quote|So&hellip;depending on who's doing the beholding, Dash is a brunette, blond, redheaded guy standing somewhere around 6 feet, who's well-built/buff/bulging with muscles, weighing in at somewhere between 150 and 250 pounds&hellip; (But look! They're all wearing the same body armor.)|Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff|<ref name="PJ9">{{WebCite|url=http://blog.bookviewcafe.com/2010/06/30/a-padawans-journal-entry-9-eye-of-the-beholder|text=A Padawan's Journal, Entry #9: Eye of the Beholder|author=[[Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff]]|work=Book View Cafe Blog|archivedate=20171123142351}}</ref>}}
The video game version of ''Shadows of the Empire'' differs from the story as told in the novel and comic versions. The game's first section, "The Battle of Hoth," focuses on Rendar's participation in that battle, which takes place before the events of the novel and comic and is only briefly mentioned in the novel. The second section, "In Search of Boba Fett," depicts Rendar's hunt for the bounty hunter after being hired by Lando Calrissian, which is also only mentioned in the novel. This section culminates in a fight between Rendar and Fett, leaving Fett's ship damaged and stuck on Gall. The [[opening crawl]] to the third section, "Hunting the Assassins," refers to the failed rescue attempt by the Rebels as shown in the novel and comic, suggesting that Rendar's own encounter with Fett occurs before the Rebels arrive in the system and he leads them to the bounty hunter. In the novel, Rendar agrees to carry the Bothan boarding party on their mission to board the ''Suprosa'' and retrieve the supercomputer containing the Death Star II plans, but the game features a mission in which Rendar personally boards the vessel and retrieves the computer.<ref name="SotE-N" /><ref name="SotE-VG" /><ref name="SotE2" />

The major differences between the game and other versions come in the fourth section, "Lair of the Dark Prince." In the novel and comic, Rendar accompanies Skywalker, Calrissian, and Chewbacca into Xizor's Palace, locating Organa and escaping moments before the palace is destroyed by a thermal detonator thrown down a garbage chute by Calrissian. In the game, however, Skywalker instructs Rendar to find a way to cover their escape while the others search for Organa. Rendar makes his own way through the sewers leading to the palace, and places [[Pulse bomb/Legends|pulse bombs]] on the service panels for the elevator connecting the palace to Xizor's skyhook, destroying the palace and cutting off the skyhook. After leaving Coruscant, the novel and comic show Rendar helping to fight Black Sun's fighters until the Imperial forces under Darth Vader destroy Xizor's skyhook, allowing them to escape. In the game, Rendar engages the skyhook in the ''Outrider'', destroying its turbolasers, before flying inside and taking out the power core. Instead of being struck by debris while escaping, in the game, Rendar appears to be killed when he fails to escape the skyhook in time before the power core is destroyed.<ref name="SotE-N" /><ref name="SotE-VG" /><ref name="SotE6">[[Shadows of the Empire 6|''Shadows of the Empire'' 6]]</ref> According to Jon Knoles, the decision to have Rendar attack the Skyhook was made "to prove he's the greatest gung-ho dude in the galaxy."<ref name="Secrets" /> Where the differing versions cannot be reconciled, this article follows the events as depicted in the novel and comic.<ref name="SotE-N" /><ref name="SotE2" /><ref name="SotE6" />

Rendar's physique varies in different sources, between his svelte depiction in [[Michael Sutfin]]'s illustration for ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'' and the muscular Rendar as shown in the Hildebrandts' paintings.<ref name="NEGTC" /><ref name="SOTECard-DashLeebo">{{Topps|set=1996 Topps Star Wars: Shadows of the Empire|cardname=Dash and Leebo|link=https://www.rebelscum.com/photo.asp?image=/sote/soteTC077.jpg}}</ref> Likewise, though his hair is generally red in color and is described as such in sources including the ''Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook'' and ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'',<ref name="NEGTC" /><ref name="SotES" /> the ''Shadows of the Empire'' and ''Shadows of the Empire: Evolution'' comics depict him with dark brown hair.<ref name="SotE:E" /><ref name="SotE2" /> These visual discrepancies were discussed by ''Shadow Games'' author Maya Kaathryn Bohnhoff in her blog.<ref name="PJ9" />

The description of how Rendar came to acquire Leebo given in ''Underworld Appendix: Swoops, Spice, and Wretched Rogues'', differs from the earlier version given in the ''Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook''. Whereas the ''Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook'' states that Rendar was given Leebo in exchange for transporting the droid's master to [[Byblos/Legends|Byblos]], ''Underworld Appendix'' says that Rendar took Leebo as his co-pilot after the droid's master, his previous co-pilot, was killed.<ref name="SotES" /><ref name="UA:SSWR" /> "''And Leebo Makes Three''" expands on these events, with Gareeda selling the droid to Rendar for passage of Rodia, although he never actually boards the ''Outrider'', and the introduction of Rendar's existing co-pilot, Eaden Vrill.<ref name="Insider128" /> [[Star Wars: The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection 1|''The Official Starships & Vehicles Collection'' 1]] also contradicts the ''Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook'', stating that Rendar personally liberated the ''Outrider''{{'s}} KGDefender engines from the [[Corulag Academy|Imperial Academy]] on [[Corulag/Legends|Corulag]]. The ''Shadows of the Empire Sourcebook'' had previously stated that the engines were acquired from Corulag by Bolabo Hujaan's agents and sold to Rendar by Hujaan.<ref name="SotES" /><ref name="OSVC1">{{StarshipsVehiclesCite|1|Starship & Vehicle Directory}}</ref>

In ''Galaxy of Fear: The Doomsday Ship'', the ''Outrider'' is erroneously called the ''Outrunner''.<ref name="Fear" /> This error was later addressed by [[Daniel Wallace]] in ''The New Essential Guide to Characters'', where it is established that the ''Outrunner'' is a separate ship and that both were owned by Rendar.<ref name="ERC" />
